source_text: Desinat nunc haereticus a Iudaeo, aspis, quod aiunt. a uipera, mutuari uenenum, euomat iam hinc proprii ingenii uirus, phantasma uindicans Christum. nisi quod et in ista sententia alios habebit auctores, praecocos et abortiuos quodammodo Marcionitas, quos apostolus Iohannes antichristos pronuntiauit, negantes Christum in carne uenisse, et tamen non. ut alterius dei ius constituerent, quia et de isto notati fuissent. : sed quoniam incredibile praesumpserant deum carnem. quo magis antichristus Marcion sibi eam rapuit praesumptionem. aptior scilicet ad renuendam corporalem substantiam Christi. qui ipsum deum eius nec auctorem carnis induxerat nec resuscitatorem, optimum uidelicet et in isto et diuersissimum a mendaciis et fallaciis creatoris. et ideo Christus eius, ne mentiretur, ne falleret et hoc modo creatoris forsitan deputaretur. non erat quod uidebatur et quod erat mentiebatur: caro nec caro, homo nec homo. proinde deus, opinor, nec deus. cur enim non etiam dei phantasma portauerit? an credam ei de interiore substantia, qui sit de exteriore frustratus? quomodo uerax habebitur in occulto tam fallax repertus in aperto? quomodo antem, in semetipso ueritatem spiritus, fallaciam carnis confundens, negatam ab apostolo lucis, id est ueritatis, et tenebrarum, id est fallaciae, commisit communicationem? iam nunc. cum mendacium deprehenditur Christi caro, sequitur, ut et omnia, quae per carnem Christi gesta sunt, mendacio gesta sint, congressus contactus conuictus ipsae quoque uirtutes. si enim tangendo aliquem liberauit a uitio uel tactus ab aliquo, quod corporaliter actum est non potest uere actum credi sine corporis ipsius ueritate. nihil solidum ab inani, nihil plenum a uacuo perfici licuit, putatiuus habitus, putatiuus actus: imaginarius operator, imaginariae operae. sic nec passiones Christi eius fidem merebuntur. nihil enim passus est qui non uere est passus; uere autem pati phantasma non potuit. euersum est igitur totum dei opus. totum Christiani nominis et pondus et fructus, mors Christi, negatur, quam tam impresse apostolus demandat, utique ueram, summum eam fundamentum euangelii constituens et salutis nostrae et praedicationis suae. tradidi enim. inquit, uobis in primis, quod Christus mortuus sit pro peccatis nostris et quod sepultus sit et quod resurrexerit tertia die. porro, si caro eius negatur, quomodo mors eius adseueratur, quae propria carnis est passio, per mortem reuertentis in terram, de qua est sumpta, secundum legem sui auctoris? negata uero morte. dum caro negatur, nec de resurrectione constabit. eadem enim ratione non resurrexit, qua mortuus non est, non habendo substantiam scilicet carnis, cuius sicut et mors ita et resurrectio est. proinde resurrectione Christi infirmata etiam nostra subuersa est. nec ea enim ualebit, propter quam Christus uenit, si Christi non ualebit. nam sicut illi, qui dicebant resurrectionem mortuorum non esse, reuincuntur ab apostolo ex resurrectione Christi, ita resurrectione Christi non consistente aufertur et mortuorum resurrectio. atque ita inanis est et fides nostra, inanis et praedicatio apostolorum. inueniuntur autem etiam falsi testes dei, quod testimonium dixerint. quasi resuscitauerit Christum, quem non resuscitauit. et sumus adhuc in delictis, et qui in Christo dormierunt. perierunt. sane resurrecturi, sed phantasmate forsitan, sicut et Christus.
pass_a_gloss: Marcion’s Christ as phantasm → flesh/man/God none of them; works and passions then lies; deny true death/resurrection and faith/preaching empty; our rising falls with his.
pass_b_english: Let the heretic stop borrowing poison from the Jew — asp from viper, as they say — and spit out from here the virus of his own wit, claiming Christ as a phantasm. Yet in this judgment too he will have other authors, premature and aborted Marcionites of a kind, whom the apostle John called antichrists for denying that Christ came in flesh — and yet not so as to set up another god’s right, since they would have been marked for that as well. But because they had presumed it incredible that God should be flesh, all the more did the antichrist Marcion seize that presumption for himself — fitter, of course, for refusing Christ’s bodily substance. For he had made his god neither author of flesh nor its raiser, best plainly in this too and most unlike the Creator’s lies and deceits. And so his Christ, lest he should lie, lest he should deceive and in that way perhaps be counted the Creator’s, was not what he seemed, and lied about what he was: flesh and not flesh, man and not man. Therefore God, I suppose, not God either. Why should he not have borne a phantasm of God as well? Am I to trust him about the inner substance when he has been frustrated about the outer? How will he be held true in what is hidden if he is found so false in what is open? How, confusing in himself the truth of spirit and the falsehood of flesh, has he joined the communication of light — that is, truth — and of darkness — that is, falsehood — which the apostle denied? Now then: when Christ’s flesh is caught as a lie, it follows that everything done through Christ’s flesh was done by a lie — meetings, touch, living together, the very powers too. For if by touching someone he freed him from a defect, or was touched by someone, what was done bodily cannot be believed truly done without the truth of the body itself. Nothing solid could be finished from what is empty, nothing full from what is void: putative habit, putative act; imaginary worker, imaginary works. So neither will his Christ’s sufferings earn faith. For he has suffered nothing who has not truly suffered; but a phantasm could not truly suffer. Therefore the whole work of God is overthrown. The whole weight and fruit of the Christian name — the death of Christ — is denied, which the apostle presses so hard as true, making it the chief foundation of the gospel and of our salvation and of his preaching. For I delivered to you first, he says, that Christ died for our sins and that he was buried and that he rose on the third day. Further, if his flesh is denied, how is his death asserted, which is the proper passion of flesh, returning through death into the earth from which it was taken, according to the law of its author? But with death denied while flesh is denied, neither will there be certainty about the resurrection. For by the same reason he did not rise by which he did not die — namely by not having the substance of flesh, whose death and resurrection alike it is. Therefore with Christ’s resurrection weakened, ours too is overturned. For it will not hold — that for which Christ came — if Christ’s does not hold. For just as those who said there is no resurrection of the dead are refuted by the apostle from Christ’s resurrection, so if Christ’s resurrection does not stand, the resurrection of the dead is taken away too. And so our faith is empty, and the apostles’ preaching empty. And even false witnesses of God are found, because they have given testimony as if he raised Christ whom he did not raise. And we are still in sins, and those who have fallen asleep in Christ have perished — sure to rise, but perhaps by a phantasm, as Christ also.

choices.why: Keeps Tertullian’s phantasma polemic term; ‘illusion’ softens the corporeal denial at stake.
putatiuus habitus/actus is forensic-putative, not mere ‘looks like’.
inanis tracks 1 Cor 15’s empty/null gospel claim.
